label: Swamp buffalo

links.name: NAST 1998: Proposal, new scientific name of the domesticated swamp buffalo, the carabao

names.text: 'Swamp-type water buffalo' is from Wikipedia's type section, which was opened. 'Carabao' is from the title of the NAST 1998 paper, seen in WebSearch result titles only, not opened.

links.name: NAST 1998: Proposal, new scientific name of the domesticated swamp buffalo, the carabao

sources.text: The name appears in the title of the NAST 1998 proposal, seen in WebSearch result titles only, not opened.

about.text: The swamp buffalo is the water buffalo type with 48 chromosomes, kept mainly for work in rice-growing areas, with a small amount of milk. In 2003 China had about 22.76 million swamp-type buffaloes and the Philippines about 3.2 million.

sources.text: Chromosomes, work and milk from the Wikipedia article. The 2003 counts for China (22.76 million, all swamp-type) and the Philippines (3.2 million swamp-type carabao) are from the populations article as fetched.

domestication.text: The swamp type originated independently in mainland Southeast Asia and was domesticated between 3,000 and 7,000 years ago.

sources.text: Place and dates from the article's swamp type section. The country list is my own mapping of mainland Southeast Asia to today's countries, not from the article.

FAO: Gateway to dairy production and products, buffaloes

sources.text: Estimated as what is left of FAOSTAT's 2023 water buffalo milk (150.69 Mt, flag A) after the river type's estimate (105.48 Mt): 150.69 − 105.48 = 45.21. The river estimate rests on the FAO gateway's 70% head share (no year) and equal milk per head. That probably overstates swamp milk, since the sources say swamp buffaloes give little milk.

facts.v: China had about 22.76 million swamp-type buffaloes and the Philippines about 3.2 million carabao.

sources.text: From the populations article as fetched, which gives both figures for 2003.

gaps: No head count for the swamp type from an opened source. The 21.8% world share (about 37.6 million, year not given) was seen in WebSearch text only and was not used. No swamp-type milk figure or yield per lactation was found in an opened source; the 2023 milk figure is a residual estimate and is probably high. No breed records from FAO DAD-IS were found.
